doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Cherokee in twelve keys, piano and Aebersold
summary: He still can play Cherokee in twelve keys, taught himself piano from 18 and likes play-alongs.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well can you still play “Cherokee” in twelve keys?
I think I can yeah. Crazily enough.
I can’t play it in one, come on now.

Oh yeah. I don’t know for some reason you had to learn that because that was one of Charlie Parker’s “Koko” you know, and it became a great exercise. In fact I used to do that even on piano because I play some piano, since I have been about 18. I didn’t have a piano until I was 18 then a neighbor next door, I got a hold of one.
Mostly self-taught. A little study with some people, Hanon and different things, mostly self-taught and always interested in the harmonies.

It definitely helps like to — and it helps when you’re playing with other people or yourself to go through tunes. I like the Aebersold things too. They’re good. You know all the things, twelve keys there again. Yeah, yeah, “Cherokee” in twelve keys, but I was doing it years ago.
